§9.4.2 Header Body Column Count Mismatch

📄 Page rule — applied from the page alone

tables-header-body-column-count-mismatch · tables columns repair

✅ Normative

Every row of a table MUST carry the full column count. Where the header and the body disagree, the short side MUST be padded with empty cells, one per missing position, and MUST NOT be padded with a duplicated or invented value.

Header:  | Duration | Factor | Trend |     ← 3 columns
Body:    | 1        | 0.94   |             ← Trend all-blank → body reads as 2
         | 2        | 0.91   |

Header wider than the body

The usual cause is a column whose body is uniform or empty — all 1.000, all blank, all —. The column MUST be restored as cells, empty where the page prints nothing, and its header label MUST be kept: a column proven only by its header still exists (Barely-Existing Columns and Headers§9.3.1).

Header narrower than the body

The usual cause is a missed span in the header: a group label that carries a colspan, or a stub that takes a rowspan. The header's spans SHOULD be re-read against the page before the body is treated as the side that is short.

Padding

  • Padding MUST be individual empty cells, one per missing position — not a span across the gap. A span claims the page merged those cells; it did not, they were simply not printed. The same reasoning pads a jagged half cell by cell in Triangles and Matrix Tables§9.8.2.
  • Body cells MUST NOT be fabricated or duplicated to reach a count. An empty cell asserts nothing; a copied value asserts something false about the page. Where it cannot be decided which side is wrong, the output renders the cells that are printed and pads with empty cells rather than guess at content.

✅ Sample — 702

The header declares four price columns ($2,000–$5,000). Rows like Corporal Punishment print one merged note — "Medical Payments Not Available" — spanning all four instead of per-column values, and parent rows such as 612. Owned Watercraft Liability Coverage print no values at all: their four value positions are empty cells. The coverage labels are indented up to three steps.
